title: Contractions: The not Family
goal: I can push two words together to make a contraction, like don't and can't.

card.desc: Bristol learns what a contraction is: two words pushed together, with an apostrophe where the letters drop out. She learns the not family (don't, isn't, aren't, wasn't, didn't, doesn't, can't), builds four of them with paper strips and sticky notes at home, and puts the apostrophe in the right spot. Contractions are one of her weak areas.

win: You did it! You can push words together like a pro!

slides.title: Contractions: On Your Own
slides.text: You learned contractions with Jonathan. Now make them on your own! ✏️

slides.title: Contractions
slides.text: A contraction is two words pushed together.

steps.text: In the not family, the o drops out. In can't, the n and o drop out.

slides.tip: The apostrophe goes where the letters were. It does not go at the end.

slides.title: Say it out loud
slides.text: Say these out loud. You can tell your mom!
prompts: Tell your mom what a contraction is.
Say is not as one word. Say did not as one word.
Find a word with n't in your book.

slides.title: Make the contraction
slides.text: Type the contraction. Put the apostrophe in the right spot.

items.no: Push does not together. Take out the letters that drop. Put in an apostrophe.

items.why: are not → aren't. The apostrophe takes the place of the o.
items.no: Push are not together. Take out the letters that drop. Put in an apostrophe.

items.no: Push can not together. Take out the letters that drop. Put in an apostrophe.

items.q:

items.why: The o drops out.
items.no: Look at not. Which letter is missing in don't?

How many letters are gone?

items.no: Count the letters of not that are missing in can't.

items.q: In wasn't, what does the apostrophe take the place of?
items.why: was not → wasn't. The apostrophe takes the place of the o.

The t is still there at the end.

items.q: The bus ____ here yet. It is late.
items.why: The bus is not here. is not → isn't.
no: aren't means are not. We say the bus is, not the bus are.
don't means do not. The bus do not here does not make sense.

items.q: We ____ have a dog. We have a cat.
items.why: We do not have a dog. do not → don't.
no: doesn't means does not. We say we do, not we does.
isn't means is not. We is not have does not make sense.

items.no: What times 6 makes 36?

items.q: There are 4 ponds. Each pond has 8 ducks. How many ducks?
items.why: Equal groups: 4 × 8. Double 8 is 16. Double 16 is 32.
items.no: Each pond has 8. Multiply. Then check your math.

teacher.objective: Bristol learns what a contraction is (two words pushed together; the apostrophe takes the place of the missing letters) and makes the not family: don't, isn't, aren't, wasn't, didn't, doesn't (the o drops out) and can't (the n and o drop out). She puts the apostrophe in the right spot and takes each contraction apart. Week 6 Day 1 (Learn it). won't waits for Thursday.
materials: Zoom with screen share (open the Class lesson from the course page, code 9110)
At her home: 6 paper strips (or index cards cut in half), a marker, 4 sticky notes (or small paper squares), her book
Paper and pencil at her home for drawing an apostrophe and a comma
Packet (2 pages) for Tia to print this week (it is due Thursday, on Tuesday's task list)

plan.do: Class slide 1. Share your screen. Check her paper strips, marker, sticky notes and book.
Class slide 2. What happened, a part where someone talks, how she knows (quotation marks).
Class slide 3. She says the answers; you tap and type.

plan.block: What is a contraction? + the apostrophe
plan.do: Class slides 4–5. Two sentences that mean the same thing; she draws an apostrophe and a comma for the camera.
Class slide 6. She makes don't with a paper strip and a sticky note.
Class slide 7. Five contractions; she makes isn't and didn't with strips.
Class slide 8. Two letters drop out (n and o).
Class slide 9. She answers and spells; you type.
Class slide 10. She names the box; you tap.
Class slides 11–12. She spells each contraction out loud, saying "apostrophe" in the right place.
Class slide 13. She finds an n't word in her book and says the two words.
Class slide 14. She reads each sentence with her choice.

plan.block: Say it both ways + quick check
plan.do: Class slides 15–16. On her own, no help.
Class slide 17. Show tonight's task list: the After-Class Lesson and 10 minutes of reading. Nothing else tonight.

watch: Putting the apostrophe before the n (did'nt, is'nt). Ask: "Which letter dropped out? Put the apostrophe where it was."
Putting the apostrophe at the end (dont'). Show the paper strip: the sticky note covers the o, in the middle.
Writing cann't or ca'nt for can't. Two letters drop out of not, so only one n is left.
Reading the contraction as the two long words (reading doesn't as "does not"). That is fine for meaning, but she should also say it as one word.
Mixing doesn't and don't ("we doesn't"). Say the long way: "we does not" sounds wrong, so it's don't.
Typed answers ignore the apostrophe (didnt is accepted on screen). When she spells out loud in class, YOU check the apostrophe spot. The packet and the multiple-choice items check the spot.

packet_key.answer: Any sentence that uses didn't correctly, with a capital letter and a period (for example: I didn't eat my peas.)
Any n't word from her book with its two words (for example: couldn't = could not). Check that the two words are right.

teacher.notes: Tonight is light on purpose: only the After-Class Lesson (it ends with Show What You Know, 3 question sets that rotate on retakes) and 10 minutes of reading. This lesson's Practice and Packet are on Tuesday's task list, due Thursday. Check her score before Tuesday. If she scores under 85, start Lesson 14 with 10 minutes of paper strips (do not, is not, did not, can not), then have her retake Show What You Know (new set) before the Lesson 14 After-Class Lesson. Engine note: the typed answers ignore apostrophes, so a typed answer without the apostrophe still counts. The apostrophe spot is checked by the multiple-choice items, the sort, and the packet.

tasks: Monday night: do the After-Class Lesson. Finish with Show What You Know.
Monday night: read your book for 10 minutes. Look for a word that ends with n't.
Tuesday or Wednesday: do the reading lesson Reading Foundations: Syllables. Clap the beats in each word and split big words into parts. Aim for 90. If it is locked, type 1111.

slides.title: Contractions
slides.text:
Some words can push together. 🤝
Today you learn how!

notes.do: Share your screen. Check that she has, next to her: 6 paper strips (or index cards cut in half), a marker, 4 sticky notes (or small squares of paper), and her book. Ask Tia to set these out before the lesson.
notes.say: "Today you learn a new kind of word. Two words push together and become one short word."
notes.ask: "Have you ever seen a word with a little mark up high in the middle of it?"
notes.listen: Any example is fine (don't, I'm, it's). If she says no, say: "You will find lots of them today."

slides.title: Who is talking?
slides.text: Think about the book you are reading.
prompts: What happened in your book since our last lesson?
Find a part where someone talks. Read it out loud.
How do you know someone is talking?

notes.do: About 6 minutes. If she finished Amy and the Missing Puppy, use the book she is reading now. She holds the page up to the camera.
notes.say: "When people talk, they use short words. Today you learn one kind of short word."
notes.ask: "Who is talking? What words did they say? How do you know?"
notes.listen: Quotation marks (talking marks) show the words someone says. If she reads the whole page, ask her to read only what the character says.

items.q: There are 3 vans. Each van has 9 kids. Which number sentence fits?
items.why: Each van has 9. Equal groups: 3 × 9 = 27.
no: Each van has 9. That is equal groups, so multiply.
There are 3 vans, not 9.

items.no: Use the 7s trick: the 5s fact plus the 2s fact.

notes.do: Zoom: she cannot tap your screen. She says the answer and you tap or type it for her. She names the trick first.
notes.ask: "Equal groups? Which operation?" "What is your 7s trick?"
notes.listen: 3 × 9 = 27; 49 (35 + 14). If a fact slipped, note it for Tuesday.

slides.title: Two words become one
slides.text: Read both sentences. They mean the same thing.

steps.text:
I do not like rain.
I don't like rain.
don't is a contraction. A contraction is two words pushed together into one word.
Some letters drop out. A little mark takes their place.

slides.tip: We use contractions all the time when we talk.

notes.do: She reads both sentences out loud.
notes.say: "These mean the same thing. The second one is shorter. Shorter words made from two words are called contractions."
notes.ask: "Which sentence is shorter? Which two words made don't?"
notes.listen: "The second one." "do and not." She says the word contraction back to you.

slides.title: Meet the apostrophe

visual.sub: The red mark is the apostrophe.

steps.text: An apostrophe sits up high, at the top of the letters.
In a contraction, the apostrophe takes the place of the missing letters.

slides.tip: Apostrophe: up high. Comma: down low.

notes.do: She draws an apostrophe and a comma on paper and holds it up to the camera.
notes.ask: "Where does an apostrophe go: up high or down low?" "What does it take the place of?"
notes.listen: Up high, like a comma floating at the top. It takes the place of the missing letters.

slides.title: Watch it happen

steps.text: 3. Put an apostrophe where the o was.

slides.tip: The apostrophe goes where the letters were. It does not go at the end.

notes.do: Hands on, at home: she writes do not on a paper strip with a space between the words. She sticks a sticky note over the o in not, draws an apostrophe on the sticky note, then pushes the two halves together and holds it up.
notes.say: "Watch the o. It drops out, and the apostrophe takes its place."
notes.ask: "Which letter did we take out? Where did the apostrophe go?"
notes.listen: "The o." "Where the o was, between the n and the t."

slides.title: The not family
slides.text: In each one, the o in not drops out.
slides.tip: Every word in the not family ends with n't.

notes.do: Reveal one at a time. She reads the two words, then the contraction. She makes isn't and didn't with paper strips and sticky notes, like don't.
notes.ask: After each one: "Which letter dropped out?"
notes.listen: The o every time. Watch for her saying "doesn't" as "does not" when she reads; have her read the contraction as one word.

slides.title: The odd one: can't

steps.text: We often write can not as one word: cannot.
So can't has only one n before the apostrophe.

slides.tip: can't: the apostrophe takes the place of n and o.

notes.do: She writes can not on a strip and covers the n and the o of not with one sticky note, then draws the apostrophe.
notes.say: "can't is the odd one. Two letters drop out, not one."
notes.ask: "How many letters did the sticky note cover? Which ones?"
notes.listen: "Two: n and o." If she writes cann't, show her the strip: only one n is left.

items.q:
is not → isn't
Which letter is gone?
items.why: The o in not drops out. The apostrophe takes its place.
items.no: Look at not. Which letter is missing in isn't?

items.q:
can not → can't
Which two letters are gone?
items.why: The n and the o in not drop out.
items.no: Look at not. Two letters are missing in can't. Which ones?

items.q: Which shows was not as a contraction?
items.why: The o drops out. The apostrophe goes where the o was: wasn't.
no: The o was between the n and the t. The apostrophe goes there, not before the n.
The apostrophe does not go at the end. It goes where the o was.

notes.do: Zoom: she says the answer and spells it. You type or tap exactly what she says.
notes.listen: o; n and o; wasn't. On the last one, she should explain why was'nt is wrong.

slides.title: Right spot or wrong spot?
slides.text: Is the apostrophe where the letters were? Tap a word. Then tap a box.

items.why: Wrong spot. The o was between n and t: isn't.
items.hint: The apostrophe takes the place of the o. Where was the o?

items.why: Right spot. The apostrophe is where the o was.
items.hint: Where was the o in does not?

items.why: Right spot. It takes the place of n and o.
items.hint: can not: the n and o drop out.

items.why: The o was between n and t. Right spot!
items.hint: Where was the o in is not?

items.why: Wrong spot. An apostrophe in a contraction does not go at the end: aren't.
items.hint: Does the apostrophe go at the end?

items.why: Right spot. The apostrophe is where the o was.
items.hint: Where was the o in are not?

items.why: Wrong spot. It should be doesn't.
items.hint: The apostrophe goes where the o was, between n and t.

items.why: Wrong spot. It should be can't.
items.hint: can stays whole. The n and o of not drop out.

notes.do: She reads each word out loud and says "right spot" or "wrong spot". You tap the word, then the box she names.
notes.ask: On each wrong one: "Where should it go?"
notes.listen: The apostrophe sits between the n and the t in every not word.

slides.title: Make the contraction
slides.text: Say it. Then spell it out loud, letter by letter.

items.why: does not → doesn't. The o drops out.
items.no: Write does, then n, apostrophe, t.

items.why: are not → aren't. The o drops out.
items.no: Write are, then n, apostrophe, t.

items.why: did not → didn't. The o drops out.
items.no: Write did, then n, apostrophe, t.

notes.do: She spells each one out loud, saying "apostrophe" where it goes. You type exactly what she spells.
notes.listen: d-o-e-s-n-apostrophe-t; a-r-e-n-apostrophe-t; d-i-d-n-apostrophe-t. Typing ignores the apostrophe, so YOU check the spot from what she says.

items.why: isn't is short for is not.
items.no: Every n't word has the word not in it.

items.why: wasn't is short for was not.
items.no: Look at the letters before n't.

items.why: aren't = are not.
no: is not makes isn't.
Look at the letters before n't: a-r-e.

notes.do: She answers out loud. You type.
notes.ask: "What word hides at the start of wasn't?"

slides.title: Contraction hunt
slides.text: Look in your book for a word that ends with n't.
prompts: Find a word that ends with n't. Spell it.
Read the sentence again with the two words.

notes.do: About 5 minutes. She looks through her book (dialogue is the best place to look) and holds up the page.
notes.say: "Be a contraction hunter. Look in the parts where people talk."
notes.ask: "What two words make it? Read the sentence the long way."
notes.listen: Any n't word. If she finds a word like Amy's, say: "That apostrophe shows who something belongs to. We will learn that another time. Today we hunt for n't." If she finds won't, say: "That one is special. We learn it on Thursday."

items.why: did not → didn't.
no: doesn't means does not.
don't means do not.

items.why: is not → isn't.
no: aren't means are not.
wasn't means was not.

items.why: are not → aren't.
no: isn't means is not.
can't means can not.

notes.do: She reads each sentence out loud with the contraction she picks, then you tap it.
notes.ask: "Read it with your word. Does it sound right?"

slides.title: Say it both ways
prompts: Say: I do not like peas. Now say it with a contraction.
Say: The dog is not big. Now say it with a contraction.
Make up your own sentence with can't.

notes.do: Quick and fun. She says each sentence both ways.
notes.listen: I don't like peas. The dog isn't big. Her own can't sentence makes sense.

items.why: do not → don't.
items.no: Take out the o in not. Put in an apostrophe.

items.why: can't is short for can not.
items.no: What word does n't stand for?

notes.do: She answers on her own, with no help. She spells don't out loud.
notes.listen: d-o-n-apostrophe-t; not. If she misses either, go back to slide 6 or 8.

notes.do: Stop sharing for the first question so she answers from memory. Then share the course page and show tonight's task list.
notes.say: "Tonight: the After-Class Lesson and 10 minutes of reading. That's all. Look for n't words when you read!"
notes.listen: Two words pushed together; it takes the place of the missing letters; can't (n and o).
